# MM-P1-L3-IH01 - Maintenance manual - Machining induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Scope
- This document defines required maintenance tasks, rationale, and acceptance criteria for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01). It is intended for maintenance technicians and process engineers responsible for upkeep of the induction heater in the P1, line P1-L3 machining cell.
- Tasks covered include inspection of the induction coil and water cooling circuit, verification of control interlocks, replacement of wear items, and functional checks after maintenance.
- Refer to ECN-2026-005 for design changes applicable to this equipment and to SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05 for operational start/stop and safety procedures.

Background and rationale
- The induction heater raises billets to the target billet temperature for downstream machining operations. Maintaining coil integrity and cooling performance prevents overheating, reduces the risk of coil failure, and preserves metallurgical quality before machining.
- The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. This value is the process requirement for the machining cell; deviations can affect part geometry and tool life.
- Coil cooling water is the primary method to remove heat from the coil assembly. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Maintaining at or above this flow prevents coil temperature rise that can lead to insulation damage and premature failure.
- This manual focuses on tasks that directly affect temperature control and cooling performance. Non-critical cleaning and housekeeping are covered in SOP-P1-L3-03.

Tools
- Multimeter capable of verifying low-voltage control signals and continuity.
- Portable flow meter compatible with the plant cooling water system for spot-check verification.
- Infrared thermal scanner for surface temperature trend checks on accessible coil housings (do not use for process temperature calibration).
- Torque tools are not specified here; use manufacturer torque requirements referenced in ECN-2026-005 where applicable.
- Insulated hand tools for electrical isolation work.
- Lockout/tagout kit per SOP-P1-L3-05.

Procedure
Preparation
- Notify production and operations per SOP-P1-L3-03 before starting maintenance. Confirm that the heater is placed in a maintenance hold condition and that material feed is stopped.
- Apply lockout/tagout following SOP-P1-L3-05 on all energy sources to EQ-P1-L3-IH01, including electrical and hydraulic supplies. Verify zero energy state before any disassembly.

Visual inspection
- Inspect coil assembly for signs of physical damage: cracks in coil housing, discoloration indicating overheating, and loosened fasteners. Replace any components found delaminated or with obvious insulation damage; consult ECN-2026-005 for replacement part references.
- Inspect cooling water hoses and connections for chafing, kinks, or leaks. Replace hoses showing wear or compromised fittings.

Cooling circuit verification
- With the system returned to a drained and isolated condition per SOP-P1-L3-05, attach the portable flow meter to a test point on the coil cooling inlet or to the maintenance bypass as allowed by plant procedures.
- Reintroduce cooling water under controlled conditions and verify flow. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. If flow is below this value, troubleshoot upstream filters, pump supply, and strainer conditions before returning to service.
- Check for proper routing of hoses to ensure there are no high points where air could be trapped; purge air as required by plant water system practice in SOP-P1-L3-03.

Electrical and control checks
- Inspect control wiring and connections for evidence of overheating or corrosion. Verify continuity of primary interlock circuits using the multimeter.
- Inspect power contactors and control relays for pitting or excessive wear; replace per ECN-2026-005 guidance where specified.
- Verify that thermal and flow interlocks are present and configured to alert or shut down when cooling flow is below the specified minimum or when coil temperatures exceed safe operating limits.

Functional verification
- After completing inspections and repairs, return the equipment to service per SOP-P1-L3-03 and SOP-P1-L3-05. Conduct a staged bring-up with close monitoring of control alarms and cooling flow.
- Confirm through process indications that billets reach the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 1235 °C as indicated by the process control system or calibrated process pyrometers. If the control system indicates difficulty attaining or holding this temperature, document deviations and escalate to process engineering with reference to ECN-2026-005.

Examples and troubleshooting guidance
- Example: If cooling flow measures below 79 L/min and strainers are clean, suspect pump cavitation or upstream valve position. Verify valve alignment and pump condition per plant pump maintenance practices and escalate if necessary.
- Example: If coil surface shows localized hot spots on thermal scan, inspect for loose coil clamps or degraded insulation and replace affected coil segments per ECN-2026-005.

Records to keep
- Maintain a maintenance log entry for each intervention that includes:
  - Equipment id: EQ-P1-L3-IH01
  - Date and revision id: Rev C
  - Description of work performed and parts replaced with reference to ECN-2026-005 when applicable
  - Measured coil cooling water flow value(s) and indication that coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min was verified
  - Verified process indication that target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C or notes on deviation
  - Names and signatures of technician and supervisor
- Retain instrument calibration records for the portable flow meter and thermal scanner used to verify conditions.
- File copies of any non-conformance reports and follow-up corrective actions linked to ECN-2026-005 references.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil cooling water flow at the measurement point meets or exceeds coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 79 L/min.
- No visible coil insulation damage or loose fasteners remain after maintenance; any replaced components are recorded with ECN-2026-005 part guidance.
- Control interlocks and alarms for cooling flow and temperature are functional and verified to actuate per SOP-P1-L3-05 during simulated fault conditions.
- Process control indicates billets reach the target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) of 1235 °C under normal operating load or documented deviations are entered and addressed with process engineering.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-005
- SOP-P1-L3-03
- SOP-P1-L3-05
